q: Why is opening a new connection for every query slow?
options: Postgres starts a new process for each connection, and it also checks the password and may set up TLS
Postgres has to rebuild every index before it can answer the first query
The query text must be compiled into machine code each time
The operating system limits you to one query per second per client
why: A connection is a whole server process. Setting it up costs time before any query runs. A pool pays that cost once and reuses the connection.

q: Your pool has 10 connections and 25 requests ask for one at the same moment. What happens to the extra 15?
options: They fail at once with an error
They wait in line until a connection is given back
Postgres opens 15 more connections on its own
They are sent to a replica
why: A pool is a queue. If the line is long, requests wait. That is why you set a connection timeout, so a request fails instead of hanging for ever.

q: You run 8 app servers. Each has a pool of 20. `max_connections` on Postgres is 100. What is the problem?
options: There is no problem, because pools share connections between servers
8 × 20 = 160 connections can be opened, which is more than 100
Each pool should be exactly 100 to match max_connections
Pools only count when they are busy, so idle servers use none
why: Total connections = app instances × pool size. Add them up and keep the sum under max_connections, with room left for admin work.

q: In PgBouncer transaction mode, which of these breaks?
options: Running a normal INSERT
Using BEGIN and COMMIT
Session state that you expect to stay between transactions, such as a SET or a session lock
Running more than one query per request
why: In transaction mode your next transaction may run on a different server connection. Anything that lives in the session does not follow you.

q: A good first guess for pool size is...
options: As big as possible, so nothing ever waits
Equal to the number of users online
Small: a few times the CPU cores of the database, split across all app servers
Always exactly 100
why: More connections than the database can work on at once only adds waiting and memory use. A small pool with a queue is usually faster.
